Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal at Novus reviewed the MSA/Order Form and we have one outstanding commercial item: limitation of liability and the consequential damages carve-out. Attached is a clean redline of the Order Form. We appreciate that Redwood historically prefers mutual carve-outs; from our side this is material to accept the SLA levels and the data residency commitments.

Can you confirm Redwood's stance and whether we can reach an acceptable compromise quickly? We have procurement deadlines next week.

Subject: RE: Limitation of Liability — proposed language

Team / Michael — thanks for patience while we reviewed. Below is Redwood's formal position and attached redline. Summary:

1) Exclusion language: Redwood will not accept a unilateral, one-way exclusion for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages. Our standard is mutual exclusion. We are willing to accept narrow, buyer-favorable carve-outs for: (a) proven breaches of confidentiality that result in third-party claims; (b) willful misconduct; and (c) statutory data protection liabilities (e.g., fines/penalties to the extent not otherwise indemnified).

2) Definition clarity: We will agree to tighten the definition of "Consequential Damages" to a short enumerated list (lost profits, loss of business, loss of data, business interruption) and include an explicit clause that excludes any recovery otherwise captured by indemnity obligations. This eliminates the broad, catch-all interpretation.

3) Cap proposal: Redwood proposes a compromise cap of 2x the first 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, whichever is greater (standard blended cap language). For data breach events covered under the carve-outs above, damages recoverable are uncapped only to the extent covered by applicable statutory liabilities or third-party judgments (we'll accept a higher sub-cap for data-related third-party claims).

4) Mechanics and fallback: If Novus insists on one-way exclusion, Redwood will require a higher cap (3x fees) and expanded warranty/insurance representations (cyber insurance confirmation and higher SLAs) — effectively a commercial trade-off.

Next steps: I've attached Redlines_MSA_Novus_v3.docx with tracked changes (Section 9: Limitation of Liability; Section 10: Definitions). Sergio/Neha — if you approve this position, I'll send to Novus legal with a short cover email outlining the commercial trade-offs and the two-path options. Michael — please let us know which path you prefer; we can also schedule a quick 30-min call to expedite.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
